name: Sheet-pan chicken fajitas
tip: Set everything in the middle of the table and let everyone build their own.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Slice chicken and peppers into strips.
Toss chicken and peppers with oil, fajita seasoning, salt and pepper. Spread across the tray in a single layer so the edges roast golden.

Roast for 20–22 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through in the thickest part. Cut into the thickest piece: it should be steaming hot throughout with no pink meat, and the juices should run clear. If unsure, continue cooking.
Finish with lime off the heat, tasting in small additions.
Warm wraps and serve with grated cheddar and soured cream.

name: Creamy garlic parmesan chicken pasta
tip: A deep pan keeps washing-up to a minimum.
method: Cut the chicken into even 2 cm pieces, finely chop the garlic, grate the Parmesan and zest the lemon before starting. Prepare the listed chicken stock.
Heat the listed oil in a deep pan. Sauté the chicken for 4–5 minutes until lightly golden, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the penne and hot chicken stock. Simmer for the pasta packet time, stirring often and adding water in small splashes whenever the pasta is no longer mostly covered; the pasta should be nearly tender before adding the cream.

Stir in the cream and simmer gently until the pasta is tender, the sauce coats it and the chicken is fully cooked. Check the thickest chicken piece reaches 75°C for 30 seconds; continue cooking if needed.
Turn off the heat and stir through the measured Parmesan. Finish with lemon zest and a little juice, tasting as you go, then season and serve.

name: Slow-cooker BBQ pulled pork buns
tip: Start it in the morning and dinner practically takes care of itself.
method: Before switching on the slow cooker, pat the pork shoulder dry. Slice the onion and crush the garlic. Rub the whole joint with smoked paprika and garlic, then set it on the onion.

Add about 150 ml BBQ sauce and the apple cider vinegar around the 1.2 kg pork shoulder. Add 100 ml water if the cooker needs a little liquid; consult its instructions. Leave the whole joint intact while it slow-cooks.
Cook on low for 7–8 hours, until safely cooked and tender enough to pull apart easily with a fork.
Shred with two forks and stir through the cooking juices. If the sauce needs thickening, simmer it uncovered briefly before filling the buns.
Fill six brioche buns with shredded pork and divide the 300 g prepared coleslaw between them. Serve extra BBQ sauce only if separately purchased.

name: Beef & three-bean chilli

Add cumin, smoked paprika and chilli powder, then stir in one 400 g tin of chopped tomatoes and beans drained and rinsed from two 400 g tins (about 480 g drained in total).

name: Honey-soy salmon & greens

method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Finely grate the ginger and crush the garlic.

method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g/2 lb loaf tin with baking parchment.
Mash the peeled bananas in a large bowl. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, melted butter and vanilla into the mashed banana.
Fold in the self-raising flour, baking powder and cinnamon just until no dry flour remains; do not overmix.
Spoon into the lined tin and bake for 55–65 minutes. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out without wet batter. Cover loosely with foil if browning too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then move to a rack for at least 10 minutes before slicing. Store covered and eat within a sensible food-safe period.

name: Soft cinnamon swirl rolls
tip: A cosy weekend bake: allow time for two rises.
method: Warm the milk until lukewarm, not hot. Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar and a pinch of salt. Add the milk, egg and 50 g softened butter and knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 60 minutes or until doubled in size.
Mix 30 g soft butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll the dough to roughly 35 × 25 cm, spread with the filling and roll up tightly from the long edge.
Cut into nine equal spirals and arrange slightly apart in a lined baking tin. Cover and rise for 35–45 minutes until visibly puffy.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Bake for 22–27 minutes until golden and cooked through in the centres.
Cool for 10 minutes. Stir the icing sugar with 1–2 tsp water and drizzle over the warm rolls.
